drafted_from: tool:pick-cover-frame's own row in tools/media-composition/tool-rows.json, tools/media-composition/do-work/save-cover-frame.mjs, tools/media-composition/test/cover-frame-unknown-duration.test.mjs (same script), and the script run on a synthetic 26 second test-pattern clip
start_here: Say to your AI: "Pick the best cover frame from my video and save it as a picture 160 pixels wide." It runs tool:pick-cover-frame and saves a JPEG in your files.
no_lists_because: It reads one video you name and saves one picture from it, so it keeps no list of its own.
instructions: 1. Find your video's identity in your files: 1f: then 64 hex.
2. Say "Pick a cover frame for this video". Add at (seconds) to use the frame at that time instead of choosing, and width in pixels (default the video's own).

3. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run and tool tool:pick-cover-frame. The door runs it in a container and answers {"result": {...}}; an error comes back as {"error": "what to change"}.
4. Read result.time (which second was chosen), result.chosen_by and files.picture, the JPEG saved in your files.

worked_examples.title: The sharpest, best-exposed frame
worked_examples.ask: Pick the best cover frame of my video, 160 pixels wide.
worked_examples.given: read from tools/media-composition/do-work/save-cover-frame.mjs and run on a 26 second 320x180 test-pattern clip; with no at it scores frames for sharpness and exposure

worked_examples.title: The frame at a time you choose
worked_examples.ask: Use the frame at 3.5 seconds as the cover.
worked_examples.given: read from tools/media-composition/do-work/save-cover-frame.mjs and run on a 7 second clip: with at given nothing is scored, so chosen_by is "the time given" and score is null
